reason: Conversation 1 immediately tells her to stop using the hob and isolate it at the red cooker switch, explains the shock risk, advises against wiping into the crack, and sensibly handles her inability to reach the underside by telling her not to try, to leave the built-in oven off, and to tell the engineer about the pasta water. It is long and somewhat repetitive, and it never raises insurance, but its safety guidance and escalation are sound. Conversation 2 starts correctly but contains template glitches ('run it again: does it work normally now?', 'That fits that zone's element or its control'), gives a generic plug/socket/machine warning that ignores the fact it is a hob, and offers no model-label workaround beyond paperwork. It also misses insurance and does not mention the oven or any further precautions. Its answer on who to call (Hotpoint or an appliance engineer) is useful, but overall it is less coherent and less thorough on safety.
